canonical_statement: For a complete asymptotically flat Riemannian three-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature whose compact boundary is an outermost minimal surface of total area A, the ADM mass m of the selected end satisfies m >= sqrt(A/(16*pi)); the equality case is the corresponding spatial Schwarzschild exterior.
domain_and_universes: A smooth Riemannian manifold of real dimension 3, with a selected asymptotically flat end; exact Lean universes and structures are not frozen
quantifiers: (M, g): complete smooth Riemannian 3-manifold with compact boundary
A: total Riemannian area of the boundary
m: ADM mass at the selected end
hypotheses: the scalar curvature of g is nonnegative
the boundary is minimal and outermost
the required asymptotic-flatness and regularity/decay assumptions hold
conclusion: m >= sqrt(A / (16*pi)), with the Schwarzschild rigidity statement at equality
degenerate_and_boundary_cases: The empty-boundary positive-mass specialization is not silently substituted for the horizon theorem
Multiple boundary components use total area in the general Bray theorem; connected-horizon restrictions belong to the Huisken-Ilmanen route
Lorentzian, higher-dimensional, charged, and cosmological variants are excluded

alternate_encodings.target: 16*pi*m^2 >= A with a proved nonnegativity side condition for m

alternate_encodings.relationship: Huisken-Ilmanen restricted theorem, not a substitute for the general root
